title: Edge-choice map tiles explainer and onboarding poster
creator: Asha Kaur
description: Create a compact, reuse-first set of UX assets for the onboarding quickstart and docs: a poster-style explainer graphic and a set of interactive map tile illustrations that show how Redwood routes requests by proximity and latency. Assets must work across the Console onboarding modal, quickstart doc hero, and a small animated SVG used in the API docs. Focus: clarity for engineers (why a nearby region reduces tail latency), fallbacks when nearest region is saturated, and the routing precedence (tier -> proximity -> cost). Avoid heavy jargon; use a visual ribbon to represent 'proximity score' and a fade-to-gray for fallback regions.
acceptance_criteria: Hero poster (1920x600 px) exported as PNG + vector SVG with layers intact, includes clear headline, 3-line subhead, and callout pointing to 'How routing works' in Console.

Set of 6 map tile SVGs (light/dark variants) showing: nearest-region hit, cross-region fallback, multi-region canary, regional outage fallback, cost-preference route, and private/VPC-only route. Each tile has an accessible text label embedded.

Animated micro-interaction for docs: 4-frame SVG demonstrating request flow (client -> edge -> region -> model replica -> fallback). Animation exported as Lottie JSON and as a looped GIF for markdown docs.
Figma file with grouped components and tokens (colors, icons, ribbon gradient) plus a short usage note for engineers on size and contrast requirements.
Assets uploaded to Drive + linked in the ticket; Console screenshot mockups with assets applied are reviewed and approved by PM.
WCAG color contrast check done for all text overlays and alt text provided for each exported image.
Design review completed with PM and Platform Eng; any required follow-ups tracked as sub-tasks.
